speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are pregnant and experiencing fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. To narrow this down, how many weeks pregnant are you, and have you noticed any rash or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old female at 30 weeks gestation. The patient presents with a sudden onset of fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. She reports the consumption of ice cream 3 days prior to the onset of symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of ice cream consumption three days prior to the onset of symptoms is highly suggestive of Listeriosis. Given your 30-week gestation and the presence of fever and headache, have you experienced any uterine contractions, vaginal bleeding, or leakage of fluid from your vagina?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever. I also have Headache, Anorexia, Fatigue, Malaise.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Listeriosis (Listeria monocytogenes infection).
The combination of maternal fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise in a 30-week pregnant patient with a history of consuming unpasteurized dairy products (ice cream) is clinically diagnostic for Listeriosis. I am requesting immediate results for a blood culture and serum Listeria monocytogenes IgM/IgG.
